column1: # The independent oracle for the Phase-6 obligation ledger.
# Authored from `documents/engineering/workflow_calculus_doctrine.md` section 3: provision
# returns a handle and a teardown obligation together, and the obligation is discharged
# either by tearing the resource down or by transferring it to a longer-lived declaration
# "with a stated condition". Nothing below is read off the ledger it judges, which is what
# lets it stay red when a workflow's accounting is wrong.
# One row per resource a workflow provisions, naming how that obligation left the
# outstanding set. The table is a *replay*: it says what the ledger of each workflow must
# come to, and the suite runs the workflow and compares.
# Three separate questions are asked of every workflow, and they are separate because they
# fail separately — which is the whole reason a single "the ledger is correct" check would
# be worth less than three:
#   balance        every resource provisioned was released and every resource released was
#                  provisioned, as sets. A dropped obligation fails this. A doubled one
#                  does not
#   multiplicity   no resource left the outstanding set twice. A doubled discharge fails
#                  this. A dropped one does not
#   condition      a row whose discharge is `transferred` must carry the condition the
#                  workflow stated, and the ledger must carry the same one. A transfer
#                  recorded as a teardown fails this and leaves both sets untouched
# A `tore-down` row carries `-` for its condition: a resource that was returned needs no
# statement about when it will be. That asymmetry is the doctrine's — a transfer is the
# arm that outlives the workflow, so it is the arm that owes an explanation.
# The five workflows are the corpus: one resource torn down, one transferred, two nested,
# two provisioned in parallel branches, and one of each in the same workflow. Between them
# every arm of the algebra runs and both discharges occur.
# workflow<TAB>resource<TAB>discharge<TAB>condition
